title: Stratified calibration packs for production prompt distributions
creator: Maya Chen
description: Curate per-domain calibration packs and a reproducible sampling strategy to feed the offline calibration workflow (FP8 / INT8 profiles). Goal: produce compact, representative packs for each business domain (search, assistant-chat, summarization, code-gen) that preserve production prompt distribution characteristics (length, tokenization artifacts, instruction structure, customer segmentation) while keeping pack sizes small enough for iterative calibration (1k-10k prompts per domain).
acceptance_criteria: Defined naming convention and metadata schema for per-domain packs (domain, date, sample-method, hash)
Sampling implementation that outputs deterministic seeds and fingerprint-based deduplication
Stratified sampling across token-length buckets, instruction templates, and customer buckets with configurable weights
Holdout set (20%) per pack for accuracy validation and regression detection
Calibration workflow consumes packs and produces FP8 / INT8 profiles that are validated against holdout with <= 1.5% median relative accuracy degradation on critical prompts
Automated CI job that runs pack generation on a recent data snapshot and publishes a diff to the calibration dashboard
implementation_notes: Fingerprinting: use Murmur3 + normalized prompt text (strip PII, collapse whitespace, canonicalize placeholders) to identify unique prompts
Reservoir + stratified sampler: for long-tail domains use per-customer reservoir sampling to avoid over-representing heavy hitters
Time decay: add recency weight (alpha parameter) so recent prompt forms have higher selection probability
Token-length buckets: 0-64, 65-256, 257-1024, >1024 (configurable per domain) to ensure coverage of model KV/cache regimes
Synthetic augmentation: small targeted augmentation (paraphrases) only for domains with <1k unique prompts after deduplication
Privacy: prompts must pass PII stripping step; originals stored in internal dataset S3 with access controls, pack files contain only prompt_id, fingerprint, metadata and anonymized prompt text
Calibration-run inputs: each pack record includes representative sampling seed, source-date, and sampling-config used so runs are reproducible
Profiling targets: collect per-token logits, calibrated scale factors, and quantization-induced PPL deltas during validation
discussion: 2025-09-16: Prototype sampler implemented (diego/samplers/stratified-reservoir). Initial results on assistant domain show over-representation of a single enterprise customer; added per-customer cap.
2025-09-18: Reviewed trade-offs with PM (Ravi Patel): agreed to prioritize domains with highest inference cost delta first (search & assistant) and defer low-volume internal tools domain to phase 2.

2025-09-22: Design feedback (June Park): preference for pack metadata UI to show coverage heatmaps by token-length and instruction-type. Linked to console design: https://confluence.redwood-ai.com/display/CONSOLE/Calibration+Pack+UX
2025-09-24: Security review kickoff: S&P flagged potential leakage in paraphrase augmentation. Decision: disable augmentation for customer-tagged prompts unless explicit consent flag present.

2025-09-28: Accuracy validation thresholds discussed with Applied ML (Anika Rao). Proposed metric: median relative accuracy change on holdout + worst-2% prompt delta. Anika requested automatic rollback if worst-2% degradation > 5%.

2025-09-30: Implemented deterministic seeding and added a --dry-run mode that emits sample diagnostics (histograms, fingerprint collisions). Sample diagnostics uploaded to dashboard: https://dash.redwood-ai.com/calibration/pack-diagnostics/ENG-15822
2025-10-01: PR opened for sampling pipeline orchestration: https://github.com/redwood-inference/calibration/pull/412 (awaiting review).
notes: We must be careful to avoid calibration packs that bias quantization toward frequent enterprise customers; sampling weights will have a per-customer cap and an amplification knob for underrepresented templates. Validation should include semantic-similarity checks (embedding cosine) to detect semantic duplicates that plain text fingerprinting misses.
